course_description: Revitalising Indigenous languages involves diverse processes, practices, and skills, that are underpinned by Indigenous ways of being, knowing and doing. In this course, students build critical knowledge and skills in four key topics in Indigenous Language Revitalisation; community and revitalisation networks, adult language learning, archival research and language description.

course_aims: This course provides students with practical and culturally-sustaining critical skills in key topics in Indigenous language revitalisation.

learning_outcomes.description: Discuss and reflect on knowledge systems, methodologies, and technologies pertinent to Indigenous language revitalisation and apply these theories in diverse contexts to reclaim Languages.
Demonstrate advanced skills in engaging with Communities, Elders, knowledge holders, and other language practitioners, enhancing networks and alliances that support language revitalisation.
Identify and evaluate culturally affirming and self-directed language learning strategies.
Articulate key theoretical approaches and concepts in linguistic description.
Locate, interrogate and appraise language and cultural material in archives and collections and contrast past and present practices and outcomes for language documentation and revitalisation.

learning_activities.topic: Pre-workshop Online Session 1 This week's session is an orientation to the program and introductions to the group.
Pre-workshop Online Session 2 We examine models for Indigenous Language Revitalisation and Sustainability through Community Language Planning Frameworks.
Pre-workshop Online Session 3 We examine models for understanding Indigenous Language Revitalisation and Sustainability through Community Language Planning and Language Vitality Frameworks.
Pre-workshop Online Session 4 We examine models for understanding Indigenous Language Revitalisation and Sustainability through Community Language Planning and Language Network Frameworks.

Pre-Workshop Online Session 5 Archival research is an important part of language planning, reclamation and revitalisation. We discuss readings and plan ahead for archival research in the intensive. Learning outcomes: L05

Monday Intensive Day 1 Session 1 Introductions - Who is in the room? Greetings in language First Nations Languages of Australia – an overview Sessions 2 & 3 Language Learning & Sharing Strategies & Goals Assignment 4
Tuesday Intensive Day 2 Session 1 Language ideologies & language networks Session 2 Sounds and spellings Session 3 Presentation & Report preparation

Wednesday Intensive Day 3 Session 1 Ownership, authority and protocols So you think you can research! Navigating collection catalogues Session 2 Technology and archival research skills Developing own language resource catalogue Session 3 Language Reference Materials Critical evaluation of these resources and their role in Indigenous Language revitalisation

Thursday Intensive Day 4 Session 1 & 2 Practical skills development – Fryer Library orientation. Applying Indigenous data sovereignty principles and Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property Protocols. Locate and view collection items Session 3 Peer Learning - Presentations and group discussion
Friday Intensive Day 5 Session 1 & 2 Peer learning - Presentations and Group Discussion Session 3 Review of assessment tasks and planning
Post-Workshop Online session 1 Debrief and follow-up. Guest speaker tba
Post-Workshop Online session 2 Linguistic description - making links to AUIL7201 Parts of speech in English. Linguistic terminology and method.
Post-Workshop Online session 3 Links to AUIL7201 - Language Description Orientation to intensive 2 Planning for your own Language studies and assessments
